about:
# LorePath

"Hold your own hand"

**LorePath** is a lightweight WoW Forever addon that maps *your* story. For every zone, dungeon, raid and battleground it draws each questline as a storyline graph, in the style of Attune's attunement paths. It shows what you've done, what you've missed and where the next part of each story starts. Click any quest to read its story.

It's not a quest helper. Its world map pins only show where quests start, and there's no objective tracking, so it sits happily alongside the default quest UI.

LorePath supports English game clients only.

> **Version 1.4.0.** Every zone, dungeon, raid and battleground now has its lore. Lore for characters, and a codex, are planned.

---

## What it shows

- **Class and Professions:** at the top of the zone list, **Class** gathers every quest for your class from all zones, so class chains that travel (say, from a capital city to another zone) show as one storyline, and so does the Tier 0.5 upgrade chain, with the steps every class shares. **Professions** has a page for each profession you have, with its quests. Their tooltips say which zone each quest is in. Quests your skill is too low for say what they need, for example *Needs Leatherworking 225*.
- **Attunements:** under **Attunements** in the zone list, a page for each chain that unlocks a dungeon or raid (Onyxia's Lair, Upper Blackrock Spire, Scholomance, Shadowforge City), with your faction's quests as one storyline across zones, and the key it ends in, ticked once you have it. They're listed by hand in `Data/Attunements.lua`, since AllTheThings doesn't model attunements.
- **Zone list:** every zone with quests your character can do, grouped by continent, each with a progress count (for example *Elwynn Forest 12/75 +3*, where "+3" is repeatable quests). Dungeons, raids and battlegrounds get their own pages under **Dungeons**, **Raids** and **Battlegrounds** headings (Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard and Library wings have their own too), and inside an instance the window opens on its page. Dungeons are listed in level order, lowest first; the rest by name. Zones, dungeons, raids and battlegrounds show WoW Forever's suggested level range in a column before the count, read from the game's Looking for Group list; hover a row for its full name, range and progress. Names are coloured by progress: grey before you start, then a gradient from red through orange and yellow to green as you go, fully green once finished. Each zone, dungeon and raid has an icon, with a tick once you've finished it, and headings show their continent's icon. Headings collapse, and a heading whose quests are all done starts collapsed (unless it holds the page you're on). The whole list can be hidden to give the graph more room.
- **Storylines:** each page's quest chains, drawn left to right from the first quest to the last, with lines joining each quest to the ones it unlocks. A storyline that starts from a quest in another zone, or goes on into one, shows those quests as faded, blue-bordered tiles at its ends, with that zone's icon (*< From Elwynn Forest*, *Continues in Westfall >*); click one to go there. Parts of one chain on a page that only meet in another zone, or that leave the page and come back, are one storyline, laid out in order. A storyline is named after its first quest, or the quest after it when that's an errand (*Speak with Ruga*) or a breadcrumb named after an NPC (*Ziz Fizziks*); one that carries on a chain from another zone keeps the chain's name. Hover its name to see which quest it starts with and, when the chain began in another zone, where. A storyline wider than the window wraps into bands, one under the other. Each storyline can be collapsed, and finished ones start collapsed. **Expand all** and **Collapse all** sit at the top.
- **About this zone and its story:** a few lines of lore at the top of a zone's page, from the Warcraft Wiki, so you know where you are before the quests begin, with its **Sources** to hover. Every zone, dungeon, raid and battleground page has one, WoW Forever's own among them. Click its header to collapse it. As you finish quests, chapters of the zone's story unlock; once one has, **Zone story** in the About header opens the side panel with the summary and every chapter you've unlocked, in story order, each with its Sources. While any chapter is still locked, the About section says there's more of the zone's story to uncover. Lore is shared across your characters: a chapter any of them has unlocked shows for all of them, with *Unlocked by * under it (each character logs in once to count); **Show spoilers** shows every chapter. A quest that has revealed a chapter gets a small book in the top right corner of its tile; hover it to read the chapter, which a storyline's **Story so far** also tells after the quest. The book and Story so far follow each character's own quests.
- **Other quests:** standalone quests with no chain, under each page's storylines.
- **Only your quests:** quests for another faction, race or class are left out. Profession quests show only if you have that profession (or, with **Show professions you don't have**, greyed out on the Professions page). Quests that come in one version per starting area, like the Shaman totem quests, show once: the version you did, else the one from your race's home. Breadcrumbs that only lead to quests you can't do are left out.
- **Quest boxes:**

  | Look | Meaning |
  | :--- | :--- |
  | Green box, ✓ | Completed |
  | Gold box, ? | In your quest log |
  | Dark box, yellow ! | Available now. The name is coloured by difficulty, as in your quest log |
  | Blue box, blue ! | Repeatable (daily and repeatable quests). Never counts toward progress |
  | Dark box, grey !, red line | Too high level, or your profession skill is too low: the line says *Lv 30* or *Needs Leatherworking 225*, and the name stays neutral instead of taking a difficulty colour |
  | Dark box, grey !, *Needs \<faction\>* | Your reputation is too low. The name keeps its difficulty colour |
  | Dimmed box, padlock | Needs an earlier quest first |
  | Dimmest box, ✗ | Skipped: a breadcrumb you went past, or a quest your reputation is now too high for |

  A small grey tick in a box's top right corner means another of your characters has finished that quest; hover it to see which. A small book there means the quest unlocked a lore chapter.

  Quests you pick up inside a dungeon or raid show its entrance portal, class quests your class icon, profession quests the profession's icon, quests started by an item that item's icon, and breadcrumbs a letter. The "?" button in the footer explains the level colours.
- **Tooltips:** hover a quest for its level, status, what it needs (earlier quests, reputation, skill), what comes before and after it, where it starts, its item rewards, which of your other characters have finished it (*Done on …*), the lore chapter it revealed (under **Lore**), and AllTheThings' note on it when there is one.
- **Quest details:** click a quest to open a panel beside the window, and click it again to close it. The panel shows:
  - requirements;
  - where it starts and who gives it, or the item that starts it and what drops or holds that item (click an outdoor one for a waypoint);
  - **Good to know:** AllTheThings' note on the quest, when it has one (where an item drops, what finishing it locks you out of, and so on);
  - its objectives and description, plus progress and completion text;
  - its item rewards (Shift+click one to link it in chat, Ctrl+click to try it on);
  - the quests before and after it, as links;
  - its address on Wowhead, to copy, at the bottom.

  **No spoilers by default:** a quest you haven't started shows "Find what awaits you." with a **Reveal** button, instead of its objectives and story. A quest in your log shows its objectives and description, but not how it ends. A completed quest shows everything. Reveal lasts until you look at another quest. **Show spoilers** in the settings shows everything always.
- **Story so far:** once you've finished a quest in a storyline, its header has a **Story so far** button. It opens the storyline's story in the side panel: each finished quest's description and completion text, in order, so you can read the chain as one story. It follows the chain across zones: finished quests on other pages that led to this storyline, or came after it, are included in order, marked with their zone. When the chain goes on to a page where you haven't done the next quest, it says where. Quests you haven't finished are left out. When the chain began on another page and you haven't done that part, it says where. A quest that revealed a lore chapter is followed by the chapter, indented under **Lore**, with the wiki articles it's from.
- **Search:** type part of a quest's name, or its ID, in the box above the zone list. The list shows up to 50 matching quests you can do, with their zone, status and level; click one to jump to it. Escape clears the search.
- **Jumping around:** in a storyline's header, click **Next**, **In progress** or **First finish** to jump to that quest, even in another zone or dungeon. **Back** returns you. An open storyline whose next quest is on the page doesn't name it in its header, since its tile is right there; collapse it, or let the quest be elsewhere, and the header says it again.
- **Waypoints:** Ctrl+click a quest, or use **Show on map** (in its details, or in a storyline's header for the next quest), to set the game's own waypoint where it starts and open the map there.
- **World map pins:** a "!" where each quest starts on the zone map you're viewing: gold for quests at your level, grey for low-level ones, red for quests you're not high enough level for yet (a blue "!" for repeatable quests at your level). Each of the three has its own entry under **LorePath quests** in the world map's filter menu, and in the settings. Only quests at your level are on by default. Quests that start at the same spot share a pin, with a count. Hover a pin for the quest's tooltip, click it to set a waypoint there, or Shift+click it to open the quest in LorePath.
- **Quest log, both ways:** for a quest you're on, **Open in quest log** in its details, or Shift+click it, opens the game's quest log at that quest. The other way, the LorePath book button on the game's quest log opens the selected quest in LorePath with its details, and the same button on a quest giver's quest dialog opens the quest it's showing.

### Controls

| Action | How |
| :--- | :--- |
| Open or close | Left-click the minimap button, `/lp`, the addons menu by the minimap, or a key binding (*Options → Key Bindings → AddOns → LorePath*) |
| Settings | Right-click the minimap button or the addons-menu entry, the **Settings** button in the window, `/lp config`, or *Options → AddOns → LorePath* |
| Find a quest | Type in the search box above the zone list; Escape clears it |
| Quest details | Click a quest; click it again to close the panel |
| Waypoint | Ctrl+click a quest, or **Show on map** |
| Open in your quest log | Shift+click a quest you're on, or **Open in quest log** in its details |
| Choose which quests show on the world map | **LorePath quests** in the world map's filter menu, or the settings page; click a pin for a waypoint, Shift+click it to open the quest in LorePath |
| Open a quest log quest in LorePath | The LorePath book button on the game's quest log, or on a quest giver's quest dialog |
| Collapse | Click a storyline's or heading's +/−, or **Expand all** / **Collapse all** |
| Hide the zone list | The arrow button left of the zone name |
| Show or hide repeatable quests | The **Repeatable** tick box, or the settings page |
| Reveal a quest's story | **Reveal** in its details; or **Show spoilers** in the settings for every quest |
| Read a storyline as one story | **Story so far** in its header (once you've finished one of its quests) |
| Show or hide the minimap button | The settings page |
| Share the quest text you've collected | **Share quest text** on the settings page, or `/lp share`, then paste the code into the [share page](https://lorepath-share.jacobhaynes49.workers.dev/) (no account needed) or a [Share quest text](https://github.com/Jacob-Haynes/LorePath/issues/new/choose) issue |
| Move the window | Drag its title bar |
| Move the minimap button | Drag it around the minimap |
| Scroll | Mouse wheel, or Shift + wheel to scroll sideways |
| Pan around a large graph | Drag with the left mouse button, from anywhere on the graph, even on a quest or a storyline header |
| Close | Escape |

`/lorepath` works the same as `/lp`, and `/lp help` lists the commands and shows your version.

### Settings

The settings page scrolls, and groups its options under three headings.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Window** | | |
| Show minimap button | On | Left-click opens LorePath, right-click opens settings. |
| Open on the zone you're in | On | Each time the window opens, it jumps to your current zone (or instance). Off: it reopens on the last page you looked at. |
| Window size | 100% | Scales the window from 60% to 140%. |
| **Quests** | | |
| Hide finished storylines | Off | Leaves out storylines where every quest is done. |
| Show standalone quests | On | Lists quests that aren't part of a chain under each page's storylines. |
| Show repeatable quests | On | Shows daily and repeatable quests, in blue. Same as the **Repeatable** tick box. |
| Show professions you don't have | Off | Lists every profession under **Professions**, with the ones you don't have greyed out and their quests locked. |
| Show quest levels on tiles | On | Shows each quest's minimum level on its tile. Quests that are too high level always show it, in red. |
| Show spoilers | Off | Shows the full story of every quest in its details, and every lore chapter. Off: quests you haven't started, and how quests in your log end, stay hidden until you press **Reveal**, and a chapter until you or one of your characters finishes its quest. |
| **World map** | | |
| Open the map when setting a waypoint | On | Opens the world map at the quest's start when you set a waypoint. |
| Show quests on the map: quests at your level | On | A gold "!" on the zone map where each quest at your level starts. Also in the world map's filter menu, like the next two. |
| Show quests on the map: low-level quests | Off | A grey "!" where quests too low to give you much experience start. |
| Show quests on the map: quests above your level | Off | A red "!" where quests you're not high enough level for yet start. |

**Reset to defaults** on the settings page puts every setting back, re-opens collapsed storylines and headings, and shows the zone list again. It keeps your saved quest text.

### What LorePath saves

Everything is saved per account in `LorePathDB` (`WTF/Account/<account>/SavedVariables/LorePath.lua`):
- **Settings:** the settings above, plus where the minimap button sits and the last page you looked at.
- **Window layout:** which storylines and headings are collapsed, and whether the zone list is hidden.
- **Quest text (`questCache`):** what the game shows you, saved as you play: description, objectives, progress and completion text. Your character's name is stored as `$N`. Gold, XP and reputation rewards are saved too, but not shown yet. So is where each quest was offered (`start`): by a creature or object (its ID) or an item, and your map and position, or just the instance when you're inside one.
- **Quests your characters have finished (`doneOn`):** for each character, the quests in LorePath's data it has finished, updated when it logs in and turns in quests, so your other characters can show them.
- **Lore unlocked (`loreUnlocks`):** each lore chapter one of your characters has unlocked, with the name of the first to do it, so your other characters can read it too.
- **Characters (`characters`):** your account's character names, with each one's class and race, so `/lp share` and `tools/merge_quest_text.py` can replace any that slip into quest text with `$N`, `$C` and `$R`.

### Sharing quest text

WoW Forever's own quests aren't in any quest database, so the only source for their story is what players see in game. LorePath saves it as you play; `/lp share` sends it to everyone:

1. Press **Share quest text** on the settings page, or type `/lp share`. A window shows a share code (it starts with `LP1:`) holding the quest text you've saved that LorePath doesn't ship yet: titles, objectives, descriptions, progress and closing text, plus gold, XP and reputation rewards, and where quests that LorePath has no start for were offered. Your character's name, class and race are replaced with `$N`, `$C` and `$R` where the text talks to you, and text LorePath already has (bundled or community text, once its placeholders are filled in) is left out; nothing else about you is in it.
2. Copy the share page's address from the window's link box into your browser: [lorepath-share.jacobhaynes49.workers.dev](https://lorepath-share.jacobhaynes49.workers.dev/). No account is needed. Click the code, press Ctrl+C, paste it there, tick the check and press **Send**. A big collection comes as several codes; paste them all, one after another. If you'd rather, paste each code into its own **Share quest text** issue on GitHub instead.
3. Either way it becomes a public **Share quest text** issue. A check replies on it with what it added, and adds the text to a pull request. Once a maintainer has reviewed and merged it, the next release has it.

---

## Where the data comes from

| Data | Source |
| :--- | :--- |
| Which quests exist, their chains, level, faction/race/class, profession and reputation requirements, repeatables, start location, quest giver, item rewards, and dungeon and raid pages | [AllTheThings](https://github.com/ATTWoWAddon/AllTheThings)' WoW Forever database (MIT), extracted into `Data/Quests.lua`: 4,434 quests on 49 zone pages and 33 instance pages (28 dungeon pages, counting Scarlet Monastery's two wings, 1 raid and 4 battlegrounds). Also each quest's starting item, where it's picked up inside an instance, and AllTheThings' notes on 92 quests, in `Data/QuestNotes.lua` |
| What you've completed, what's in your log, your level, race, class, faction, professions and reputation | The game client, live |
| Quest, zone, item, NPC and faction names | The game client, in your language |
| Level ranges of zones, dungeons, raids and battlegrounds | The game client's Looking for Group list, live |
| Zone lore | Summarised by hand from the [Warcraft Wiki](https://warcraft.wiki.gg/) (CC BY-SA 4.0), WoW Forever's own articles first, in `tools/lore/zones.txt`, built into `Data/Lore.lua`; checked for wiki changes weekly |
| What drops or holds an item that starts a quest, with chances and locations | [pfQuest](https://github.com/shagu/pfQuest)'s item, creature and object data (MIT, originally from VMaNGOS), in `Data/QuestStarts.lua`: sources for 56 item-started quests |
| Quest text: description, objectives, progress and completion text | In this order:
1. **What you've seen:** saved from the game as you play (when a quest giver shows a quest, when you accept it, when you hand items in, at the turn-in screen, and your quest log at login).
2. **Community text:** `Data/CommunityText.lua`, collected by players, including WoW Forever's own quests (288 quests so far).
3. **The game's own quest-link tooltip:** the quest's goal and requirements, even for quests completed long ago.
4. **Bundled vanilla text:** [pfQuest](https://github.com/shagu/pfQuest)'s English quest database (MIT, originally from VMaNGOS), in `Data/QuestText.lua`: 3,285 vanilla quests, not WoW Forever's own. |

Missing quests, or wrong chains, levels or start points, come from AllTheThings' Forever data. Please report them to AllTheThings too, so everyone benefits. Wrong or missing quest text is LorePath's own.

### Updating the quest data

```bash
pip install lupa
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/ATTWoWAddon/AllTheThings.git att
(cd att && git sparse-checkout set db/Camelot)
python3 tools/extract_att.py att
```

`tools/extract_att.py` loads AllTheThings' Forever zone, dungeon and raid, profession and PvP data (`Categories/Zones.lua`, `Instances.lua`, `Professions.lua` and `PVP.lua`, plus header names from `LocalizationDB.lua`) in a sandboxed Lua runtime, then writes the quest records LorePath needs to `Data/Quests.lua` and AllTheThings' quest notes to `Data/QuestNotes.lua`.
- **Kept:** repeatable quests, flagged `rp`.
- **Skipped:** quests AllTheThings marks unavailable, and quests added after or removed by Forever's build.
- **Faction versions:** a quest with separate Alliance and Horde versions keeps both, in `fv`.
- **Chains filled in:** a prerequisite AllTheThings marks unavailable keeps its place, with the quests before it added in front, so the chain doesn't break where nobody can see it. A quest with no faction of its own takes one when its start item is sold only by one faction's vendors, or when all its prerequisites are one faction's (as AllTheThings or a vendor says, not as inferred here), unless its races include the other faction's.
- **Recorded:** the headers of `Data/Quests.lua` and `Data/QuestNotes.lua` name the AllTheThings commit the data came from.

To see what changed, compare against the committed file:

```bash
git show HEAD:Data/Quests.lua > /tmp/Quests.old.lua
python3 tools/diff_quests.py /tmp/Quests.old.lua Data/Quests.lua
```

The [Sync quest data from AllTheThings](https://github.com/Jacob-Haynes/LorePath/blob/main/.github/workflows/sync-att-data.yml) workflow does this every Monday, or on demand from the Actions tab:
- **If the quest data changed,** it opens or updates a PR from the `data/att-sync` branch with the summary.
- **It fails instead** if the quest count drops by more than 10%, a zone disappears, the data doesn't load, or the tests fail. The tests include a check for quests that would show twice (see [Tests](#tests)).
- **Merging and releasing stay manual.**
- **Repository setting:** opening the PR needs *Settings → Actions → General → Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests* turned on.

`Data/QuestText.lua`, the bundled vanilla text, is a one-off import and isn't part of the weekly sync, because vanilla quest text doesn't change. `python3 tools/extract_pfquest.py` rebuilds it if ever needed, for example after new vanilla quests appear in `Data/Quests.lua`. Likewise `python3 tools/extract_quest_starts.py` rebuilds `Data/QuestStarts.lua`, where item-started quests' items come from, after the quest data gains new ones. And `python3 tools/extract_breadcrumb_npcs.py` rebuilds `Data/BreadcrumbNPCs.lua`, the names of the NPCs each breadcrumb is about, after the quest data gains breadcrumbs: a breadcrumb named after one of them (Ziz Fizziks) doesn't name its storyline. Until it's rerun, a new breadcrumb names its storyline as before.

### Updating the zone lore

```bash
python3 tools/wiki_lore.py fetch
python3 tools/wiki_lore.py status
python3 tools/wiki_lore.py build
```

Zone lore is written by hand in `tools/lore/zones.txt`: for each page, its map ID, the wiki articles it's summarised from (`source: <title> @ <revision>`, each credited in game) and a few sentences. `fetch` refreshes `tools/lore/wiki/`, a snapshot of each source's text plus the list of WoW Forever's own articles, and reports what needs a look; `status` gives the same report without fetching; `build` writes `Data/Lore.lua`. A snapshot only changes when its article's text does.

- **Weekly:** `.github/workflows/sync-wiki-lore.yml` runs `fetch` every Monday and, if the wiki changed, opens or updates a PR from `data/wiki-lore` with the new snapshots and the report: summaries whose articles changed (with a link to the wiki's diff), new Forever articles, and Forever articles no summary uses yet. Update the summaries on that branch or after merging. The workflow leaves the branch alone once someone else has pushed to it.
- **Premise and chapters:** a zone's summary is its premise, setting only, so it spoils nothing. What a storyline reveals goes in a chapter: `after <quest ID> <quest name>`, then the chapter's own `source:` lines and text, shown in game only once the character has finished that quest (all of them with **Show spoilers**). In game a chapter is read in the Zone story panel (and in its storyline's Story so far), once that character or any of the account's characters has finished its quest; the About section shows only the premise, and says "More of 's story to uncover" ("Tirisfal Glades'" for a name ending in s) while any chapter is locked, naming no quest. Each chapter is credited under its own **Sources**. `build` refuses a chapter whose quest isn't in `Data/Quests.lua`, and `fetch` and `status` report a chapter whose quest-article source is about a different quest (`fetch` reads the ID from the article's Questbox into its snapshot as `quest:`). Every zone with lore has chapters for its main storylines.
- **Adding a zone:** add an entry with its sources and empty revisions (`source: Riverglades @`), run `fetch`, write the summary from the snapshots, and fill in each revision from its snapshot.
- **Write for WoW Forever:** its own articles come first (Forever zone, instance and subzone articles, and its quests' articles, which hold most of what Forever changed; the wiki's articles on the original zones don't cover Forever). Use the original zone's article for what Forever kept, and leave out what came after vanilla (the Cataclysm, the burning of Teldrassil).
- **Requests:** `fetch` names LorePath in its User-Agent, asks for 20 articles at a time and waits between requests, as the wiki asks of scripts.

### Adding players' quest text

Shared codes arrive as **Share quest text** issues, from the issue form or from the share page (`share/`, a Cloudflare Worker that opens the issue under the maintainer's account; see [share/README.md](https://github.com/Jacob-Haynes/LorePath/blob/main/share/README.md)). The `Add shared quest text` workflow (`.github/workflows/community-text.yml`) runs on each one:
- it merges the code into `Data/CommunityText.lua` with `tools/merge_quest_text.py --replace`, so later submissions replace earlier wording for the same quest (wording usually only changes when the game does), except that text which only fills in a placeholder never replaces it;
- runs the tests, commits to the `data/community-text` branch, and opens or updates one PR from it;
- replies on the issue with what was added.

Review the PR's text before merging, especially the class and race words the report lists: they may be the sharing player's own. The workflow needs two things set up once:
- a `quest-text` label, which the issue form applies: `gh label create quest-text --description "Quest text shared with /lp share"`;
- **Settings > Actions > General > Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests**, the same setting the AllTheThings sync needs.

To add the quest text someone has collected to `Data/CommunityText.lua`, so everyone gets it in the next release, take their saved file (`WTF/Account/<account>/SavedVariables/LorePath.lua`), or your own, and run:

```bash
python3 tools/merge_quest_text.py --dry-run path/to/LorePath.lua   # see what it would add
python3 tools/merge_quest_text.py path/to/LorePath.lua
```

What it does:
- **Scope:** only adds text for quests LorePath knows, and never overwrites existing community text unless you pass `--replace`.
- **Clean-up:** strips character names (to `$N`), colour codes and links, and skips text the bundled vanilla text already has.
- **Rewards:** carries saved gold, XP and reputation rewards over too.
- **Safety:** loads each file in a sandbox with no Lua libraries.

Review the diff before committing. A saved file also contains the player's character names and settings.

### Tests

```bash
pip install lupa
python3 tools/test/run_tests.py
```

This runs the addon's Lua against a fake WoW API with the real quest data, as characters of several races and classes (Human, Orc, Tauren and WoW Forever's own race among them), about 600 checks in all. It covers:
- eligibility, reputation, repeatable quests, faction versions and one version per starting area;
- quest statuses and storyline building;
- zone, dungeon, raid, battleground, Class, profession and attunement pages, and level ranges;
- storylines that cross zones, joining parts of a chain that meet in another zone, their names and where their chains start, and wrapping long storylines to the window;
- the zone list: icons, progress colours and collapsing;
- search, jumping and **Back**, and dragging the graph;
- the detail panel, its text sources, notes and spoiler hiding;
- quest icons, the quest log both ways and linking rewards;
- saving and sharing quest text and where quests start, with your class and race put back as placeholders, including the merge tool, the share page, and where starting items come from;
- world map pins: which quests get one, grouping, colours, tooltips, clicks and refreshing;
- waypoints, the minimap button, slash commands and every setting;
- **Reset to defaults**;
- error safety: any error the addon catches fails the run;
- the quest data extractor's chain rules (hidden prerequisites and inferred factions);
- quests in the data twice (below).

It can't check how things look in game.

**Quests in the data twice.** AllTheThings sometimes has one quest under two IDs (Amongst the Ruins was 908 and 6921), so it showed once as done or in your log and once as still available. The tests look for quests with the same name on one page that one character could have together (same faction or none, overlapping races and classes) and that aren't steps of one storyline or versions of each other. When one turns up, usually after an AllTheThings sync, the test lists the pair and someone decides once:
- **one quest twice:** add it to `EXTRA_VERSIONS` in `Core.lua`, so only one shows;
- **really two quests** (a quest for each faction's cloth quartermaster, say): add it to `SEPARATE` in `tools/test/run_tests.py`, with a comment saying why.

The test also fails if a `SEPARATE` entry is no longer needed, so the list stays short. Quests with no name in LorePath's text (about 900, mostly WoW Forever's own) can't be checked this way.

---

## Installing

1. **Get it:** install from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/1793930) (or the CurseForge app), or download the latest release zip from GitHub Releases. Cloning this repository also works, but brings the `tools` and `media` folders along.
2. **Copy it:** put the `LorePath` folder into WoW Forever's `Interface/AddOns` folder. To find it, in the Battle.net app, pick WoW Forever, click the gear icon, choose **Show in Explorer** (**Show in Finder** on macOS), and open the Forever folder.
3. **Start it:** start the game, or `/reload`, and type `/lp`.

## Releasing

1. Bump `## Version` in `LorePath.toc` and add the release to `CHANGELOG.md`.
2. Push a tag (`v*`). [BigWigsMods/packager](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager) builds the addon, attaches it to a GitHub Release and uploads it to CurseForge.
   - **CurseForge:** project 1793930, set by `## X-Curse-Project-ID` in `LorePath.toc`, using the `CF_API_KEY` repository secret.
   - **Release type:** tags containing "beta" or "alpha" upload as beta or alpha files; other tags are full releases.
   - **Release notes:** `CHANGELOG.md`.
   - **Left out of the package:** `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `tools` and `media`.

## Licence

LorePath is MIT-licensed. Its bundled data:
- **`Data/Quests.lua`** and **`Data/QuestNotes.lua`** are derived from AllTheThings, also MIT-licensed. Its licence is in `Data/AllTheThings-LICENSE.txt`.
- **`Data/QuestText.lua`** and **`Data/QuestStarts.lua`** come from pfQuest (MIT, licence in `Data/pfQuest-LICENSE.txt`), which took the data from the VMaNGOS project.
- **`Data/CommunityText.lua`** was collected in game by LorePath's players.
- **`Data/Lore.lua`** (and its source, `tools/lore/zones.txt`) is summarised from the [Warcraft Wiki](https://warcraft.wiki.gg/) and, like the wiki's text, is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0, not MIT, as are the article snapshots in `tools/lore/wiki/`. Each entry names its articles; the notice is in `Data/WarcraftWiki-LICENSE.txt`.

The quest text itself is Blizzard's.

# Changelog

## 1.4.2

- **Latest AllTheThings data:** 335 more quests, among them 159 in a new zone and 16 in two new dungeons, and updated rewards, prerequisites, factions or start points for 37 more.

## 1.4.0

Everything from the 1.4.0 betas (details below), plus lore for every page. The highlights:

- **Lore for every page:** every zone, city, dungeon, raid and battleground opens with a short summary of its lore as it is in WoW Forever, from the Warcraft Wiki, with **Sources** to hover for the articles it came from.
- **Zone story:** as you finish quests, chapters of each page's story unlock, 458 in all. **Zone story** in the About section opens them in the side panel, in order, and a line says when there's more to uncover. A storyline's **Story so far** tells its chapters after their quests, and a small book marks a quest that unlocked one. **Show spoilers** shows every chapter.
- **Lore shared across your characters:** a chapter any of your characters has unlocked shows on all of them, marked *Unlocked by *.
- **Wowhead link:** each quest's details end with its Wowhead address to copy, in place of WarcraftDB's.
- **Tidier storyline headers:** an open storyline no longer repeats **Next:** for a quest whose tile is right there.

Since 1.4.0-beta7:

- **Lore for every page:** every zone, city, dungeon, raid and battleground now has its own summary and, where its quests tell a story, chapters to unlock: 458 in all, across the Eastern Kingdoms, Kalimdor, the classic dungeons, Onyxia's Lair and WoW Forever's own Riverglades, Shen'dralas and new dungeons. The chapters you and your characters have unlocked are read in the side panel instead: **Zone story** in the About header opens the whole story so far, in order, each chapter with its Sources. Chapters no longer appear under the storylines. A storyline's **Story so far** still tells its chapters after their quests, and the small book on a tile still marks a quest that unlocked one.

## 1.4.0-beta6

- **Lore in the storylines:** a zone's chapters now appear under the storylines they belong to, so the About section stays short: its opening lines, and a line while there's more to uncover. A finished storyline stays collapsed but keeps its chapter showing. A chapter with no storyline on the page shows in the About section instead. Each chapter has its own **Sources**.
- **Simpler unlocking:** a chapter shows once you or any of your characters has finished its quest, or with **Show spoilers**. The Reveal button for other characters' chapters is gone, and the "more to uncover" line now shows whenever any of the zone's chapters is still locked.

- **The whole zone story:** every zone with lore now tells its main storylines in chapters as you finish them, not just one or two. Mulgore's opening lines no longer blame the Grimtotem for the poisoned wells (in this era it was the Venture Company), and Teldrassil's no longer give away what the Crown of the Earth chain reveals.

- **Wowhead link:** a quest's details now end with its Wowhead address to copy, in place of WarcraftDB's.

Zephras Isle's lore now tells who the Skyborne are, and gains chapters for the Al'Aketh cult and the Windshapers' road to the Horde.
